Appendix E Generalization Analyses for Linear Classification

In this section, we provide supplementary generalization analyses for the linear classification experiments in Section 3.2.3. We follow the notations in Section 3.1. Let the input distribution 𝒟X\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{X}}, and the ground-truth label y∗​(𝒙)y^{*}({\bm{x}}) be sign⁡(𝒙⊤​𝒘∗)\sign({\bm{x}}^{\top}{\bm{w}}^{*}) for an unknown 𝒘∗∈ℝd{\bm{w}}^{*}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}. For a training set S=(𝒙1,…,𝒙n)S=({\bm{x}}_{1},\dots,{\bm{x}}_{n}), we define yi:=y∗​(𝒙i)y_{i}:=y^{*}({\bm{x}}_{i}) for all i∈[n]i\in[n].

E.1 Preliminaries

We base our generalization analyses on Rademacher complexity.

Definition E.1.

Given a family of functions ℱ\mathcal{F} mapping from ℝd\mathbb{R}^{d} to ℝ\mathbb{R}, the empirical Rademacher complexity of ℱ\mathcal{F} for a set of samples S=(𝐱1,…,𝐱n)S=({\bm{x}}_{1},\dots,{\bm{x}}_{n}) is defined as

ℜ^S​(ℱ)=𝔼σ1,…,σn∼unif⁡{±1}​[supf∈ℱ1n​∑i=1nσi​f​(𝒙i)].\hat{\mathfrak{R}}_{S}(\mathcal{F})=\mathbb{E}_{\sigma_{1},\dots,\sigma_{n}\sim\mathrm{unif}\{\pm 1\}}\left[\sup_{f\in\mathcal{F}}\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\sigma_{i}f({\bm{x}}_{i})\right]. (34)

Rademacher complexity is useful in deriving margin-based generalization bounds for classification. The following bound is standard in the literature Koltchinskii and Panchenko 2002, Mohri et al. 2018.

Theorem E.2 (Theorem 5.8, Mohri et al. 2018).

Let ℱ\mathcal{F} be a family of functions mapping from ℝd→ℝ\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R}. q>0q>0. For any δ>0\delta>0, with probability at least 1−δ1-\delta over the random draw of S=(𝐱1,…,𝐱n)∼𝒟XnS=({\bm{x}}_{1},\dots,{\bm{x}}_{n})\sim\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{X}}^{n}, the following bound for the test error holds for all f∈ℱf\in\mathcal{F}:

𝔼x∼𝒟X[𝟙[y∗(𝒙)f(𝒙)≤0]]≤1n∑i=1n𝟙[yif(𝒙i)≤q]+2qℜ^S(ℱ)+3log⁡(2/δ)2​n.\mathbb{E}_{x\sim\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{X}}}[\mathbbm{1}_{[y^{*}({\bm{x}})f({\bm{x}})\leq 0]}]\leq\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\mathbbm{1}_{[y_{i}f({\bm{x}}_{i})\leq q]}+\frac{2}{q}\hat{\mathfrak{R}}_{S}(\mathcal{F})+3\sqrt{\frac{\log(2/\delta)}{2n}}. (35)

Let ℱp={𝒙↦⟨𝒘,𝒙⟩:‖𝒘‖p≤1}\mathcal{F}_{p}=\{{\bm{x}}\mapsto\left\langle{{\bm{w}}},{{\bm{x}}}\right\rangle:\|{\bm{w}}\|_{p}\leq 1\} be a family of linear functions on ℝd\mathbb{R}^{d} with bounded weight in LpL^{p}-norm. The following theorem from Awasthi et al. 2020 bounds the empirical Rademacher complexity of ℱp\mathcal{F}_{p}.

Theorem E.3 (Direct Corollary of Corollary 3 in Awasthi et al. 2020).

For a set of samples S=(𝐱1,…,𝐱n)S=({\bm{x}}_{1},\dots,{\bm{x}}_{n}), the empirical Rademacher complexity of ℱ1\mathcal{F}_{1} and ℱ2\mathcal{F}_{2} is bounded as

ℜ^S​(ℱ1)\displaystyle\hat{\mathfrak{R}}_{S}(\mathcal{F}_{1}) ≤1n​2​log⁡(2​d)⋅(∑i=1n‖𝒙i‖∞2)1/2,\displaystyle\leq\frac{1}{n}\sqrt{2\log(2d)}\cdot\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n}\|{\bm{x}}_{i}\|_{\infty}^{2}\right)^{1/2}, (36)
ℜ^S​(ℱ2)\displaystyle\hat{\mathfrak{R}}_{S}(\mathcal{F}_{2}) ≤1n​(∑i=1n‖𝒙i‖22)1/2.\displaystyle\leq\frac{1}{n}\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n}\|{\bm{x}}_{i}\|_{2}^{2}\right)^{1/2}. (37)

E.2 Generalization Bounds for Sparse Linear Classification

Let 𝒟X\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{X}} be the uniform distribution on unif​{±1}d\mathrm{unif}\{\pm 1\}^{d}. Let k=𝒪⁡(1)k=\mathcal{O}(1) be a positive odd number. We draw 𝒘∗{\bm{w}}^{*} as follows: randomly draw the first kk coordinates from unif​{±1}k\mathrm{unif}\{\pm 1\}^{k}, and set all the other coordinates to 00.

Theorem E.4.

With probability at least 1−δ1-\delta over the random draw of the training set S=(𝐱1,…,𝐱n)S=({\bm{x}}_{1},\dots,{\bm{x}}_{n}), for any linear classifier f:ℝd→ℝ,𝐱↦⟨𝐰,𝐱⟩f:\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R},{\bm{x}}\mapsto\left\langle{{\bm{w}}},{{\bm{x}}}\right\rangle that maximizes the L1L^{1}-margin γ1​(𝐰):=mini∈[n]⁡yi​⟨𝐰,𝐱i⟩‖𝐰‖1\gamma_{1}({\bm{w}}):=\min_{i\in[n]}\frac{y_{i}\left\langle{{\bm{w}}},{{\bm{x}}_{i}}\right\rangle}{\|{\bm{w}}\|_{1}} on SS, the following bound for the test error holds:

𝔼x∼𝒟X[𝟙[y∗(𝒙)f(𝒙)≤0]]≤4k⋅2​log⁡(2​d)n+3log⁡(2/δ)2​n.\mathbb{E}_{x\sim\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{X}}}[\mathbbm{1}_{[y^{*}({\bm{x}})f({\bm{x}})\leq 0]}]\leq 4k\cdot\sqrt{\frac{2\log(2d)}{n}}+3\sqrt{\frac{\log(2/\delta)}{2n}}. (38)

Proof.

It suffices to consider the case where ‖𝒘‖1=1\|{\bm{w}}\|_{1}=1 because rescaling 𝒘{\bm{w}} does not change the test error. Since 𝒘∈arg​max⁡γ1​(𝐰){\bm{w}}\in\argmax\gamma_{1}({\bm{w}}), γ1​(𝒘)≥γ1​(𝒘∗)=1k\gamma_{1}({\bm{w}})\geq\gamma_{1}({\bm{w}}^{*})=\frac{1}{k}. By defintion, this implies yi​f​(𝒙i)≥1ky_{i}f({\bm{x}}_{i})\geq\frac{1}{k}. Letting q:=12​kq:=\frac{1}{2k} and applying Theorem E.2, we have

𝔼x∼𝒟X[𝟙[y∗(𝒙)f(𝒙)≤0]]≤4k⋅ℜ^S(ℱ1)+3log⁡(2/δ)2​n.\mathbb{E}_{x\sim\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{X}}}[\mathbbm{1}_{[y^{*}({\bm{x}})f({\bm{x}})\leq 0]}]\leq 4k\cdot\hat{\mathfrak{R}}_{S}(\mathcal{F}_{1})+3\sqrt{\frac{\log(2/\delta)}{2n}}. (39)

By Theorem E.3, ℜ^S​(ℱ1)≤1n​2​log⁡(2​d)⋅n=2​log⁡(2​d)n\hat{\mathfrak{R}}_{S}(\mathcal{F}_{1})\leq\frac{1}{n}\sqrt{2\log(2d)}\cdot\sqrt{n}=\sqrt{\frac{2\log(2d)}{n}}. Combining this with (41) completes the proof.

Theorem E.5.

With probability at least 1−δ1-\delta over the random draw of the training set S=(𝐱1,…,𝐱n)S=({\bm{x}}_{1},\dots,{\bm{x}}_{n}), for any linear classifier f:ℝd→ℝ,𝐱↦⟨𝐰,𝐱⟩f:\mathbb{R}^{d}\to\mathbb{R},{\bm{x}}\mapsto\left\langle{{\bm{w}}},{{\bm{x}}}\right\rangle that maximizes the L2L^{2}-margin γ2​(𝐰):=mini∈[n]⁡yi​⟨𝐰,𝐱i⟩‖𝐰‖2\gamma_{2}({\bm{w}}):=\min_{i\in[n]}\frac{y_{i}\left\langle{{\bm{w}}},{{\bm{x}}_{i}}\right\rangle}{\|{\bm{w}}\|_{2}} on SS, the following bound for the test error holds:

𝔼x∼𝒟X[𝟙[y∗(𝒙)f(𝒙)≤0]]≤4k​dn+3log⁡(2/δ)2​n.\mathbb{E}_{x\sim\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{X}}}[\mathbbm{1}_{[y^{*}({\bm{x}})f({\bm{x}})\leq 0]}]\leq 4\sqrt{\frac{kd}{n}}+3\sqrt{\frac{\log(2/\delta)}{2n}}. (40)

Proof.

It suffices to consider the case where ‖𝒘‖2=1\|{\bm{w}}\|_{2}=1 because rescaling 𝒘{\bm{w}} does not change the test error. Since 𝒘∈arg​max⁡γ2​(𝐰){\bm{w}}\in\argmax\gamma_{2}({\bm{w}}), γ2​(𝒘)≥γ2​(𝒘∗)=1k\gamma_{2}({\bm{w}})\geq\gamma_{2}({\bm{w}}^{*})=\frac{1}{\sqrt{k}}. By defintion, this implies yi​f​(𝒙i)≥1ky_{i}f({\bm{x}}_{i})\geq\frac{1}{\sqrt{k}}. Letting q:=12​kq:=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{k}} and applying Theorem E.2, we have

𝔼x∼𝒟X[𝟙[y∗(𝒙)f(𝒙)≤0]]≤4k⋅ℜ^S(ℱ2)+3log⁡(2/δ)2​n.\mathbb{E}_{x\sim\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{X}}}[\mathbbm{1}_{[y^{*}({\bm{x}})f({\bm{x}})\leq 0]}]\leq 4\sqrt{k}\cdot\hat{\mathfrak{R}}_{S}(\mathcal{F}_{2})+3\sqrt{\frac{\log(2/\delta)}{2n}}. (41)

By Theorem E.3, ℜ^S​(ℱ2)≤1n⋅n​d=dn\hat{\mathfrak{R}}_{S}(\mathcal{F}_{2})\leq\frac{1}{n}\cdot\sqrt{nd}=\sqrt{\frac{d}{n}}. Combining this with (41) completes the proof.

In this section, we give the detailed proof of results in Section 3.3.3.

For convenience, we use 𝑷k\bm{P}_{k} to denote 𝑷𝒙k\bm{P}_{{\bm{x}}_{k}}. Define 𝜽t=(𝑼t,𝑽t){\bm{\theta}}_{t}=({\bm{U}}_{t},{\bm{V}}_{t}), 𝑾t=𝑼t​𝑼t⊤−𝑽t​𝑽t⊤\bm{W}_{t}=\bm{U}_{t}\bm{U}_{t}^{\top}-\bm{V}_{t}\bm{V}_{t}^{\top} and fi​(𝜽)=⟨𝑾t,𝑷i⟩f_{i}({\bm{\theta}})=\left\langle\bm{W}_{t},\bm{P}_{i}\right\rangle, and our goal is to minimize the function Equation 5. All local minima of ℒ\mathcal{L} are global.

At any saddle point (𝐔s,𝐕s)(\bm{U}_{s},\bm{V}_{s}) of ℒ\mathcal{L}, there is a direction (𝓔𝐔,𝓔𝐕)\left(\bm{\mathcal{E}}_{\bm{U}},\bm{\mathcal{E}}_{\bm{V}}\right) such that

minimize‖𝑼‖F2+‖𝑽‖F2s.t.𝑼​𝑼⊤−𝑽​𝑽⊤=𝑾∗.\mathrm{minimize}\quad\|\bm{U}\|_{F}^{2}+\|\bm{V}\|_{F}^{2}\quad s.t.\quad\bm{U}\bm{U}^{\top}-\bm{V}\bm{V}^{\top}=\bm{W}^{*}. (53)

‖𝑼∗‖F2=tr​𝑼∗​𝑼∗⊤=∑i=1tbi\|\bm{U}_{*}\|_{F}^{2}=\mathrm{tr}{\bm{U}_{*}\bm{U}_{*}^{\top}}=\sum_{i=1}^{t}b_{i}

and similarly

Thus ‖𝑼∗‖F2+‖𝑽∗‖F2=∑i=1sbi=‖𝑾‖∗\|\bm{U}_{*}\|_{F}^{2}+\|\bm{V}_{*}\|_{F}^{2}=\sum_{i=1}^{s}b_{i}=\|\bm{W}\|_{*}. On the other hand, for any (𝑼,𝑽)(\bm{U},\bm{V}) satisfying 𝑼​𝑼⊤−𝑽​𝑽⊤=𝑾∗\bm{U}\bm{U}^{\top}-\bm{V}\bm{V}^{\top}=\bm{W}^{*}, we have

We can now prove that (𝑼∗,𝑽∗)(\bm{U}_{*},\bm{V}_{*}) is a global minimizer of ℒ\mathcal{L}, which completes the proof of Theorem F.3. Indeed, for any (𝑼,𝑽)(\bm{U},\bm{V}) we have

ℒ⁡(𝑼,𝑽)≥ℒ^​(𝑼​𝑼⊤−𝑽​𝑽⊤)≥ℒ^​(𝑾∗)=ℒ⁡(𝑼∗,𝑽∗).\mathcal{L}(\bm{U},\bm{V})\geq\hat{\mathcal{L}}(\bm{U}\bm{U}^{\top}-\bm{V}\bm{V}^{\top})\geq\hat{\mathcal{L}}(\bm{W}^{*})=\mathcal{L}(\bm{U}_{*},\bm{V}_{*}).

The last step follows from Claim 2 and Equation 44.

Lemma F.4.

[Watson 1992, Example 2] Let 𝐀=𝐋​𝚺​𝐑⊤\bm{A}=\bm{L}\bm{\Sigma}\bm{R}^{\top} be its singular value decomposition, then we have

∂∥𝑨∥∗={𝑳𝑹⊤+𝑬:‖𝑬‖≤1,𝑳⊤𝑬=0 and 𝑬𝑹=0}.\partial\|\bm{A}\|_{*}=\left\{\bm{L}\bm{R}^{\top}+\bm{E}:\left\|\bm{E}\right\|\leq 1,\bm{L}^{\top}\bm{E}=0\text{ and }\bm{E}\bm{R}=0\right\}.

It is well-known that under cerntain regularity conditions on the ground-truth matrix 𝑿∗{\bm{X}}^{*}, the global minimizer of the convex problem Equation 42 is close to the ground-truth 𝑿∗{\bm{X}}^{*}. Here we present a version of this result adapted from [Candes and Plan 2010, Theorem 7].

Theorem F.5.

Suppose that rank⁡(𝐗∗)=r=𝒪⁡(1)\mathrm{rank}({\bm{X}}^{*})=r=\mathcal{O}(1), 𝐗∗=𝐕𝐗∗​𝚺𝐗∗​𝐕𝐗∗⊤{\bm{X}}^{*}={\bm{V}}_{{\bm{X}}^{*}}{\bm{\Sigma}}_{{\bm{X}}^{*}}{\bm{V}}_{{\bm{X}}^{*}}^{\top} is (a version of) its SVD, and each row of 𝐕𝐗∗{\bm{V}}_{{\bm{X}}^{*}} has ℓ∞\ell_{\infty}-norm bounded by μd\sqrt{\frac{\mu}{d}}, then if the number of observed entries satisfies n≳μ4​d​log2​dn\gtrsim\mu^{4}d\log^{2}d, then we have that ‖𝐖∗−𝐗∗‖F≲λ​‖𝐗∗‖∗​μ2​log⁡d\|{\bm{W}}^{*}-{\bm{X}}^{*}\|_{F}\lesssim\sqrt{\lambda\|{\bm{X}}^{*}\|_{*}}\mu^{2}\log d with probability ≥1−d−3\geq 1-d^{-3}.
